person: Rosa Villanueva is a 64-year-old retired school cafeteria manager in Texas. She and her husband own their home, a rental duplex and a lot, and she handles the property taxes and insurance. This fall the servicer's annual escrow analysis on the house raised her mortgage payment, though she believes the tax bill went down and the insurance got cheaper. She keeps a folder of papers per property and wants each property named the way she names it. Her husband says 'just pay it', but she wants every line checked. She is wary of the tax consultant her neighbour uses, who keeps a share of savings, and wants to know what everything costs.
stated_up_front: My house payment went up after the escrow letter came, but the tax bill and the insurance both went down, so I don't see why. I have all the papers right here for the house. Can you check it line by line and tell me what's wrong, and please don't sign me up with anybody who takes a cut.

facts.truth: The house she and her husband live in; not the duplex or the lot, which are handled separately and are not escrowed.
The mortgage payment went from $1,684 to $1,862 a month, effective December 1.

facts.about: This year's county tax bill for the house
facts.truth: $5,240, down from $5,610 last year. The servicer's analysis still projects $5,610.
This term $1,980 with Lone Star Mutual, down from $2,310 last year; the analysis still uses $2,310.
The servicer paid the $1,980 premium from escrow in September, and her card was also charged $1,980 a few days later when the autopay renewal ran.
The analysis shows a $96 late penalty paid out of escrow on the January tax installment, but her county receipt shows it arrived on time.
She has a flood policy of $740 a year that renewed this year at $812. The analysis projects $812, which is correct.
A $430 supplemental bill came for a new pool the previous owner permitted. It is real and was paid.
A $325 umbrella policy that she pays by card herself, never through escrow.
A letter from an escrow audit firm offering to keep 35% of any refund, and a $149 'tax relief' company letter that sounds official; she has answered neither.

unknowns: Whether the cushion the servicer kept is over the legal limit of one-sixth of the year's bills
How many days the servicer has to refund a surplus and from when the clock starts
Whether the servicer was ever sent the new tax bill and insurance renewal, and when
What the 'shortage' line on the analysis means and whether it is allowed
